authority.purpose: Binding product-art-direction input for R1-R7; it does not create a second theming system or own program progress. R7 reference postures are non-product fixtures owned by customization-model.json and do not become tenant targets here.
authority.executor: Claude after an explicitly authorized round

sharedSystemLaws: Both tenants use the same public React family and stable DOM parts.
Differences travel through BrandTheme or TenantThemeDocument, validated profiles, semantic channels, recipes, anatomy, emphasis and private family values.
No tenant selector, tenant conditional TSX, second compiler, second icon supplier or app-owned clone is allowed.
A visual lane may create a private proposal but never a public --ds-* token.
Allowlisted Advanced token overrides are a governed high-precedence tier of the same system, not a second authority; they may author exact tenant values when Standard dials are intentionally coarse.
Recipe profiles and expressive experience profiles remain two independent closed registries and two independent selections; no proposal may merge them into a combined profile language.
Status colors remain semantic and accessible even when brand chrome is monochrome.
Texture, motif, gradient and motion never carry required meaning and honor reduced-transparency, reduced-motion, forced-colors and contrast floors.
The round does not invest in dark mode; tenant identity must be complete in the canonical light product posture.
The reference is a product grammar, not permission to copy logos, names, proprietary assets or exact protected trade dress.
The current BitHire and The Management palettes are migration inputs, not accepted target palettes; R1 replaces and sightedly readjudicates both through canonical authorities.

targets.paletteRebuildLaw: Replace the current technical pale-blue treatment with a restrained cool near-neutral canvas, clean work surfaces, deep readable ink and one disciplined professional-blue action hierarchy. Saturated borders, pervasive blue wash and default-control paint are forbidden.
targets.northStar: A credible, approachable and information-rich hiring workspace with the immediate familiarity of a leading professional network, expressed as BitHire rather than a literal LinkedIn clone.
currentContradictions: The theme currently selects rottay/technical-sharp@1 and rottay/bithire-technical@1.
The active profile is sharp, hairline, flat and motif-free, which over-indexes on an engineering instrument instead of a professional-network product.
Current tables and dense chrome can read as one technical grid instead of people, roles, relationships and activity.
Pill usage and blue paint exist, but hierarchy, material and composition do not yet create the requested product identity.

inspiration: dense but breathable list and search workflows
mustRemainOriginal: exact spacing, radii, typography and motion recipes

palette.canvas: cool pale neutral with clear white work surfaces
palette.brand: confident medium professional blue; selected and primary actions use blue deliberately, not everywhere
palette.ink: deep blue-charcoal with readable cool-gray supporting roles
palette.semantic: status roles remain independently accessible and never collapse into the primary blue
palette.rule: color establishes professional-network familiarity but cannot be the only divergent axis

typography.posture: humanist product sans with friendly clarity rather than technical small-caps everywhere
typography.hierarchy: strong person or record title, compact metadata, readable body, tabular numeric roles and explicit support text
typography.labels: sentence case by default; uppercase restricted to true micro-labels
typography.contentLaw: names, roles, actions and statuses do not wrap per character or disappear behind inaccessible ellipsis

geometry.controls: compact rounded rectangles; pills reserved for filters, status and compact identity chips
geometry.silhouette: cards and panels feel friendly without becoming bubbly

edges.selection: blue indicator, inset tint or contained current state; never several competing rails
edges.dividers: low-contrast structural rules with stronger boundaries only at region changes

material.posture: white contained surfaces over a cool canvas
material.depth: one restrained elevation model: subtle keyline plus low soft shadow for floating or interactive regions
material.forbidden: heavy glass, glossy bevels, stacked shadows, decorative gradients across every card

backgroundMotif.posture: optional faint connection-node, network or soft radial wash in non-content zones
backgroundMotif.contentSafeZone: motif opacity falls to zero behind text, tables and controls
backgroundMotif.fallback: solid semantic canvas under reduced transparency or forced colors

densityRhythm.behavior: density changes row and region rhythm causally while preserving controls, actions and readable person metadata
densityRhythm.grid: people and activity content receive priority; low-value metadata discloses or reflows before it compresses

icons.wells: quiet pale-blue wells for identity or key action groups, not every icon

motion.timing: short product transitions with gentle ease-out; no bounce-heavy choreography
motion.meaning: selection, disclosure, reorder, relationship and saved-state continuity
motion.reducedMotion: immediate final state with only short functional opacity where necessary

navigation.desktop: professional app shell with recognizable current destination, clear hiring-flow grouping and restrained search prominence
navigation.mobile: simplified destination set plus bottom navigation or focused action sheet; never the desktop sidebar squeezed into 390px
navigation.currentState: blue-backed or blue-indicated with persistent text and icon meaning

dataAndWorkflow.tables: person-first column hierarchy, soft header ground, calm rows, visible focus, accessible selected state and mobile card or priority projection
dataAndWorkflow.cards: profile, activity and evidence blocks with one dominant signal per region
dataAndWorkflow.filters: search and saved views remain findable without forming a wall of pills
dataAndWorkflow.charts: professional reporting grammar: quiet grid, direct labels, clean tooltip and restrained blue-led series system

responsiveComposition.desktop: sidebar or contextual rail, stable work canvas and optional detail peek compose without stealing table width
responsiveComposition.tablet: secondary rail becomes overlay or disclosure before core data compresses
responsiveComposition.mobile: identity summary, primary action, status, next step and recent activity lead; tables become task-specific list cards or sheets

governedIntegration.requiredResolution: R0 starts compose-first with the existing humanist type axis, authored typography, chrome, recipes and anatomy. It may propose a new versioned recipe selection or expressive experience profile only if a causal canary proves that the independent existing selections cannot express a reusable cross-family posture. It may not silently mutate the meaning of a published profile or treat the two registries as one.

forbiddenOutcomes: literal LinkedIn logo, copy, assets or exact trade-dress duplication
blue recolor with unchanged technical geometry and composition
dense desktop table squeezed into mobile
tenant-specific CSS selector or BitHire component branch

targets.paletteRebuildLaw: Replace teal, sandstone, terracotta and soft SaaS paint with paper or near-white grounds, near-black ink, deliberate grayscale hierarchy, ruled separation and accessible semantic exceptions. The result must be independently desirable, not a degraded BitHire.
targets.northStar: A black, white and paper-toned executive workspace: minimal, square, editorial and deliberately rustic, like a precise working dossier rather than a recolored SaaS dashboard.
currentContradictions: The DB canary currently authors teal, sandstone and terracotta.
It selects rottay/editorial-round@1, whose pill controls, round geometry and elevated surfaces oppose the requested square posture.
The current experience profile is soft, soft-depth, contour and spacious rather than crisp monochrome ledger.
The static design-intent fixture uses warm Art Deco gradients, glass and expressive shadows that must not define the new direction.

palette.canvas: paper white or very light warm gray
palette.brand: near-black, charcoal and grayscale; no decorative brand hue
palette.ink: near-black primary, dark gray secondary, mid-gray muted with explicit contrast floors
palette.semantic: success, warning, error and info remain governed semantic exceptions; combine restrained color with label, icon, pattern or shape so brand chrome remains monochrome
palette.rule: no teal, terracotta or warm multicolor Art Deco identity in the accepted target

typography.posture: editorial display or sharp grotesk paired with neutral body and mono or tabular accents
typography.hierarchy: large but restrained section titles, compact ledger labels, precise numbers and generous readable body leading
typography.labels: small caps or uppercase only for editorial metadata, with bounded tracking and no excessive all-caps body copy
typography.contentLaw: long titles reflow by region; tabular data remains aligned and accessible

geometry.controls: square or lightly eased rectangles; pills limited to unavoidable semantic compact tags
geometry.silhouette: hard rectangles, clipped editorial bands and deliberate grid alignment

edges.hierarchy: hairline internal dividers, stronger region keylines and occasional double or offset editorial rule
edges.selection: black fill with white ink, underline, bracket or ruled marker; never a blue SaaS glow

material.depth: separation is led by rules, offsets and ground changes; shadows are absent or hard and minimal
material.forbidden: glass, blur, soft floating-card soup, glossy gradients, neon glow or decorative elevation stacks

backgroundMotif.posture: subtle paper grain, ruled grid, registration marks, hatch or dossier-index motif in non-content zones
backgroundMotif.contentSafeZone: patterns never cross text or controls and disappear at small containers
backgroundMotif.fallback: solid paper ground for reduced transparency, print and forced colors

densityRhythm.posture: editorial whitespace at the region level with precise compact rows inside data regions
densityRhythm.behavior: rhythm changes gutter, rule cadence and group spacing without creating empty dead tracks
densityRhythm.grid: asymmetric editorial grids are allowed only when intrinsic and content-complete; narrow containers stack to a dossier sequence

icons.posture: thin or regular monochrome line weight
icons.wells: square outline or black inverse wells reserved for key categories and actions

motion.timing: snap or restrained ease; no spring, bounce, shimmer-led personality or floating hover spectacle
motion.meaning: rule reveal, panel disclosure, ledger insertion, selection and sort continuity

navigation.desktop: ruled index or black inverse rail with strong section labels and square current-state treatment
navigation.mobile: compact dossier index and square action sheet; prioritize current work, search and next action
navigation.currentState: black/white inversion or explicit rule, not hue

dataAndWorkflow.tables: ledger grammar with strong header rule, aligned numbers, monochrome states plus non-color markers and a clean mobile record stack
dataAndWorkflow.cards: dossier sections and framed facts rather than floating rounded cards
dataAndWorkflow.filters: compact squared controls and typographic active state
dataAndWorkflow.charts: grayscale series separated by dash, marker, hatch and direct label; no color-only differentiation

responsiveComposition.desktop: editorial regions may use asymmetry, rule-led columns and dossier side notes while keeping the primary task dominant
responsiveComposition.tablet: secondary dossier facts collapse into ruled disclosure before main content narrows
responsiveComposition.mobile: single-column working dossier ordered by decision priority, square sheets and persistent primary action; no miniature desktop grid

governedIntegration.requiredResolution: R0 composes the target first through the current independent recipe and expressive registries plus the governed Advanced tier. Exact --ds-radius-sm/md/lg/xl and --ds-color-success/warning/error/info values are already legal DB tokenOverrides and are not constrained by the Standard radiusScale envelope. If a reusable posture still cannot be expressed, recipe and expressive additions are proposed separately as versioned entries; one combined id or mutation of editorial-round is forbidden.

forbiddenOutcomes: warm Art Deco recolor presented as the new monochrome direction
round elevated cards or pill-first recipe
removal of semantic status meaning to force literal grayscale
texture behind content or required meaning encoded only by texture
tenant-specific CSS selector or The Management component branch

acceptanceQuestions: Can an observer identify the tenant in three seconds after captures are converted to grayscale?
Would each tenant still feel distinct if its primary hue were temporarily neutralized?
Do type scale, density and content length change composition without overlap, clipping, character wrapping or unjustified holes?
Does mobile preserve each identity through task ordering, chrome, rhythm and anatomy rather than only color?
Does every difference resolve from the governed tenant/profile chain rather than an app or tenant selector?

r0MechanismDecisions.envelopeLaw: The vertical and selected experience profile bound six Standard dials. Exact allowlisted Advanced tokenOverrides are a separate governed route and are not silently clamped to those dial ranges.

exactRadius.standardDial: shape.radius-scale remains bounded by the vertical and selected-profile envelopes
exactRadius.law: Use the bounded Standard dial for ordinary customization and the existing allowlisted Advanced route for an exact premium identity; family literals remain forbidden.

semanticToneSeeds.frontierAdmission: Open palette.status-seeds only if the ordinary Standard editor must expose independently authored status seeds with shared compiler derivation and contrast enforcement. It is not an architecture prerequisite for the Advanced TMM canary.

profileRegistries.newEntryLaw: A new entry composes existing vocabulary first. New vocabulary requires its own consumer, two useful postures, fallback, static-DB lowering, evidence and drill.

existingAxesFirst.motion: Use intensity, durationScale and ambient off before proposing snap or a new easing vocabulary.

productDomainBoundary.genericDataTableResponsibility: stable cells, priority projection hooks, responsive cards, selection and lifecycle
productDomainBoundary.law: Do not add recruiting-specific recipe semantics to the generic DS.

kimiProposalBoundary.allowedWrites: new proposal files under the inbox only
kimiProposalBoundary.forbiddenWrites: all product code, roadmap, program contracts, token contracts, generated output and existing annotation files
kimiProposalBoundary.retentionLaw: delete each raw submission after the DT reproduces and incorporates accepted observations into canonical contracts
kimiProposalBoundary.claudeMayConsume: canonical parent program files only; never raw or retained Kimi submissions
